scope: Bounded Zstandard codec, standalone .zst, TAR.ZST/.tzst, ZIP method 93, application operations, HTTP persistence and browser workflows. Current archive implementation and all archive tests are fingerprinted below.

original_complete_product.edition: Official complete Windows x64 installer, 7-Zip 26.04; executable tests use privately extracted command-line program 7z.exe and 7z.dll.

manual_binding.binding: English manual extracted from official complete installer 7-zip.chm; complete offline baseline manifest and feature inventory bind these bytes to the release.

original_complete_product.authentication: Installer, bootstrap and extracted 7z.exe/7z.dll hashes checked before any private original execution. Digest equality is not a signature or reproducible-build claim.
original_complete_product.direction_limit: This official product supports Zstandard and ZIP93 decoding but does not encode either. No original-generated ZSTD claim; complete GUI and shell were not exercised.

acquisition.downloads: Pinned official release URLs, exact byte counts and SHA256 authenticated before exclusive local writes; existing authenticated local backups are preferred.
acquisition.publication: Vendor executables remain ignored and excluded. Application code never imports the bootstrap or invokes an original program.

independent_encoder.authentication: Exact executable SHA256 and reported version checked, then a private copy is invoked only by tests/fixture producer.
independent_encoder.fixtures: bsdtar --format=raw/pax --zstd independently produces standalone and TAR.ZST inputs. ZIP method93 envelope is independently constructed using native node:zlib CRC32, without importing application modules.
independent_encoder.retention: Frozen compressed bytes, payload, producer and provenance retained in fixtures/zstd. Pinned Windows encoder executable is an OS component, not bundled in the repository; frozen inputs remain portable.

positive_comparisons: Candidate standalone .zst -> authenticated complete 7-Zip t/x -so -> exact independently retained binary payload.
Candidate classic ZIP93 and ZIP64+signed descriptors -> authenticated complete 7-Zip t/x -so -> exact binary and Unicode-named file bytes.
Candidate TAR.ZST -> original outer t/x -so -> exact inner TAR bytes -> original inner TAR t/x -so -> exact binary and Unicode-named file bytes.

Independent pinned bsdtar raw/PAX Zstandard -> candidate decode -> exact binary payload; original outer decode matches candidate TAR bytes and original inner TAR extraction matches payload. Fresh generated and frozen inputs both checked.
Independent ZIP93 envelope around pinned bsdtar payload -> candidate and original decode exact bytes.
Standard concatenation with skippable metadata -> candidate and original decode joined firstsecond contents.
HTTP create/list/test/extract for .zst, .tar.zst, .tzst and ZIP93+ZIP64 survives host restart; ZIP/TAR.ZST modification dates are listed/restored, standalone basename policy applied.

Native decoder verifies genuine compression with ratio below one-quarter on the independent 16416-byte mixed binary fixture at levels1,3,9,19. This is one fixture property, not a general performance comparison.
malformed_refusals: Every truncated prefix of a valid checksummed frame
Reserved descriptor flag, reserved block type, impossible block size
Nonzero dictionary ID and excessive history window
Unsafe eight-byte declared content size and malformed skippable size
Corrupt content checksum, trailing garbage, corrupt/truncated later concatenated frames
Cumulative output, container input, frame count and block count bounds; unknown-size expansion limit
ZIP93 CRC/size failures and withdrawn method20 refusal
Unsafe TAR.ZST path, unconfirmed extraction, existing archive/destination; no new extraction destination/staging on malformed input

browser_verification.limitations: In-app browser surface unavailable; recovered using connected Chrome. Full-page screenshot initially timed out; supported viewport capture succeeded. No screenshot-only inference of byte identity; files were separately hashed.

limits: Native synchronous in-memory codec; no large streaming extraction, async workers, cancellation or compression parallelism.
Node standard-library ZSTD API is experimental in the tested Node24.16.0 runtime; no cross-version guarantee.
Explicit frame walking is required because the tested native one-shot decoder stopped after its first frame and ignored trailing bytes.
No dictionaries supplied, no legacy/magicless ZSTD frames, no withdrawn ZIP method20 alias, no archive encryption or multi-volume support.

Zstandard content checksum is optional XXH64 low32, not CRC32 or cryptographic authentication; checksums present are verified. Candidate creation emits checksums. Skippable-only streams decode empty; their metadata is ignored.
Standalone .zst stores no filename/timestamp; archive basename becomes the extracted filename. TAR.ZST uses existing bounded TAR metadata rules and rejects links/sparse/devices/ACL restoration.
Independent native executable checks are Windows-only and skipped elsewhere; portable frozen fixture/parser tests remain.
No full 7-Zip feature parity, original GUI binding, exhaustive interoperability, adversarial review, optimal compression or speed improvement claim.
